Intermittent DNS resolution failures for internal services

Users in the Chicago office were trying to reach internal services by the hostname svc.internal.corp, but DNS resolution intermittently returned different A records after a same-day zone edit performed by network engineer David Kowalski (emp ID NE-40821). Some clients resolved the new address 10.10.5.21 and connected successfully, while others received the previous IP 10.10.4.9 and application requests to internal endpoints failed by name. The issue was first reported by Maria Chen (mchen@corplabs.com) at approximately 15:00 UTC. Impact was limited to internal services in corp-datacenter-1 and caused inconsistent connectivity and elevated DNS lookup failures in Network Monitoring dashboards.

Internal host failing to resolve

Engineering users in the Arlington office were trying to reach internal-app.company.local on the internal network, but between 09:12 and 09:40 EST the hostname intermittently failed to resolve and client systems received NXDOMAIN responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) via the #dns-ops Slack channel and affected access to the internal application by name through the BIND 9 cache cluster (cache-east-01.infra.company.local / cache-east-02.infra.company.local) in the us-east-1 primary datacenter. Investigation tied the failures to an outdated internal DNS A record pointing to the decommissioned IP 10.22.4.17 instead of the current 10.22.8.55, and delayed remediation because the runbook referenced a deprecated DNS change-control policy (POL-DNS-2019, superseded by POL-DNS-2025).
